entries.title: Entering the Allen School
body: I'm excited to share that I will be joining the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering at the University of Washington next quarter.
I will officially become a computer science student and continue building toward work in human-centered design and software development.

entries.title: Joining Thermo Fisher Scientific
body: I'm happy to share that I am joining Thermo Fisher Scientific as a Software Engineering Intern in Shanghai.
I will contribute to YOLO26-based vision for robot-assisted tube handling, 3500Dx localization testing, and QANTIS workflow analysis.

map.name: shanghai-map.case
map.title: Quality of Life in Shanghai
map.copy: An eight-person mixed-methods project that studied older neighborhoods, then translated community observations into a walking-time map and public information campaigns.

details.label: FIELD SIGNAL
details.copy: Respondents reported an average 6.75 / 10 familiarity with nearby stores and amenities.

details.label: INTERFACE
details.copy: A fixed map combined facility categories with 5-, 10-, and 15-minute walking filters and an early detail-panel interaction.

details.label: OUTSIDE THE SCREEN
details.copy: The team also produced food-safety and anti-fraud interventions for older residents.

details.label: EVIDENCE LIMIT
details.copy: The map was a prototype; no formal user testing or long-term quality-of-life outcome was established.

allocation.name: course-allocation.py
allocation.title: Automatic and Satisfactory Course Assignment
allocation.copy: A capacity-constrained assignment pipeline designed around four separate criteria: automation, efficiency, fairness, and the probability of receiving a preferred course.

details.label: MECHANISM
details.copy: Ranked preferences → Simultaneous Eating → fractional matrix → Birkhoff decomposition → concrete assignment.

details.label: ITERATION
details.copy: Version 2 redistributed residual probability by balancing remaining course and student capacity instead of choosing leftover courses randomly.

details.label: REPORTED RESULT
details.copy: Maximum-weight realization reached about 70% top-two and 92% top-three assignments in the original presentation.

details.label: TRANSFER
details.copy: The framework was later adapted to a parent–teacher meeting time-slot allocation problem.

emg.name: emg-monitor.device
emg.title: Monitoring Device for Muscle Usage & Behavior
emg.copy: A working embedded prototype designed to make target-muscle recruitment observable during exercise—not merely to display a raw waveform.

details.label: DESIGN DECISION
details.copy: EMG was selected over angular-displacement sensing after subtle contractions proved difficult to observe through changes in skin geometry.

details.label: CURRENT CHAIN
details.copy: Filter → square → Kalman filter → individual reference → four bands → session percentage output.

details.label: PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
details.copy: The current STEP artifact contains one solid body with source bounds of approximately 30.79 × 58.00 × 10.00.

details.label: CURRENT LIMIT
details.copy: The measurement layer works; the polished visualization, adaptive calibration, and exercise interpretation layers remain in development.

research.title: How does agreement on principles affect perceived relevance?
research.copy: Turning ethical-case survey responses into a shared quantitative representation that can be analyzed without erasing the original metadata.
research.quote: STATUS: THE BROADER SIMILARITY–RELEVANCE QUESTION REMAINS OPEN.

details.label: TRANSFORMATION
details.copy: Parse comma-separated principle labels, count occurrences, normalize by the row total, and construct ordered principle vectors.

details.label: TOOL DIVISION
details.copy: Python and pandas for transformation; Google Sheets for subsequent formulas; R for regression analysis shared with the team.

details.label: CURRENT RESULT
details.copy: The present linear models did not detect principle agreement changing with principle frequency for the principles examined.

details.label: CONTRIBUTION
details.copy: Data transformation and empirical analysis—not authorship of the lab’s ethical-principle taxonomy.

internship.title: Software Engineering Internship
internship.copy: Responsibilities span laboratory automation, localized scientific-software validation, workflow analysis for interface design, and technical enablement for team onboarding.

details.label: LABORATORY AUTOMATION
details.copy: Built the perception layer for automated laboratory tube handling with YOLO26-based object detection. Connected detection output to ROS2 robot-arm workflows for tube grasping and placement.

details.label: F1 / 3500Dx
details.copy: Executed black-box dynamic workflow test cases for F1 on the 3500Dx instrument. Clarified expected behavior and product workflows when test cases required additional context.

details.label: QANTIS
details.copy: For the QANTIS project, analyzed WinTrace, the previous EDXRF software. Documented page transitions and interaction paths in Miro to support the redesign.

details.label: INTERN ONBOARDING
details.copy: Onboarded a new intern to the testing environment. Set up the virtual machine, provided software training, resolved setup issues, and supported the transition to independent testing.
